newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's insurance giant to invest in funds.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's insurance giant to invest in funds.

text.p: Indonesia's state-owned insurance company PT Jaminan Sosial Tenaga Kerja (Jamsostek) plans to invest 1.7 trillion ($708 million) in mutual funds, Manpower Minister Abdul Latief said on Monday.
Latief said Jamsostek would invest part of its assets, presently parked in banks, in mutual funds to gain higher returns.
"We have selected 10 securities firms to invest our money in investment funds," Latief said, adding that the companies were seleceted from among 200 securites firms.
He said the performance of the selected firms would be reviewed periodically and the three worst performers would be replaced annually.
Latief said Jamsostek posted a net profit of 106 billion rupiah ($44 million) in 1996, up from 81 billion rupiah ($34 million) in 1995 and 62 billion ($26 million) in 1994.
"We forecast 128 billion rupiah for 1997," he said.
Jamsostek, the largest insurance company in Indonesia, has 15.8 million registered members at present, up from eight million in 1993.
